Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11

Interface WindowLifecycleListener

All Known Implementing Classes:
CompositedWindowBridge
public interface WindowLifecycleListener
The window-manager lifecycle seam the conventional 2D desktop subscribes to so that native X11 applications appear as ordinary windows inside the 2D desktop.

X11WindowManager already drives the 3D texture path on Map/Unmap/Configure/PropertyNotify. This listener is the parallel, presentation- agnostic notification: whenever a redirected client window is mapped, resized, retitled, activated or unmapped, the WM fires the matching callback so a desktop-side controller can open/adjust/close the hosting window. The 2D shell adapts it to Desktop2DCompositorHost (see CompositedWindowBridge), which in turn obtains each window's Swing surface from a CompositedWindowHost.

Callbacks are invoked on the X event-dispatch thread. Implementations that touch Swing must marshal to the EDT themselves (the 2D bridge does). The WM isolates each callback in a try/catch, so a desktop-side failure is logged and never kills the X event loop.

Deliberately free of gnu.x11 and Java 3D types — it speaks only in window ids, titles and pixel sizes — so the desktop2d package can implement it without dragging in the scene graph or the X protocol objects.
